summary: All 18 KJV quotes verify verbatim and the Christ-typology/grace-anchored CTA are doctrinally sound, but the Beat 1 revelation scene contradicts the source by placing the 'I am Joseph' disclosure before 'ten' brothers when Scripture has eleven (Benjamin included) present at that moment.

findings.beat: Beat 1 — 'But on that day, ten travel-worn men came begging me for grain... And when I could hold it in no longer... I am Joseph your brother, whom ye sold into Egypt.'
findings.quote_or_claim: But on that day, ten travel-worn men came begging me for grain, not knowing the ruler they bowed to. They were my brothers ... And when I could hold it in no longer, I sent every Egyptian out of the room ... I am Joseph your brother, whom ye sold into Egypt.
findings.problem: The narration telescopes two separate visits and carries the count 'ten' into the revelation scene. The 'I am Joseph your brother' disclosure (Gen 45:1-4) happened on the SECOND journey, with all ELEVEN brothers present, including Benjamin (Gen 43:15-16; 44:14). The 'ten' brethren without Benjamin describes the FIRST grain-buying visit (Gen 42:3-4), at which no disclosure occurred. Stating that Joseph revealed himself to 'ten' men contradicts the text, which has eleven present at that saying.
findings.proposed_fix_text: But on that day, my brothers came begging me for grain, not knowing the ruler they bowed to — the very brothers who had sold me, whose faces I had carried in the dark for half my life. And when I could hold it in no longer, I sent every Egyptian out of the room, and I wept aloud until the house of Pharaoh heard me, and I said the words they had dreaded for twenty years:
